Inject a failure mode on a machine, now or at a simulation time
post.description: The machine breaks down with the code as its cause and raises its alarm, as in a natural failure. It takes effect only while the machine is Running; otherwise it is held and applied where the machine would next enter Running (#140). With `at` it is scheduled as a simulation event, so a live run reproduces a headless run with the same injections. 404: unknown machine or code; 409: `at` in the past or on a calendar boundary, or the run has finished.

post.summary: Inject a leak-test sensor drift, from now or a simulation time until a time
post.description: Adds `shift` to the leak tester's readings from `at` until `until` or the tester's next calibration, whichever comes first (#196, ADR-0033). No random draw changes, so the readings without the drift are exactly the logged ones minus `shift`. The event log gets a `leak-drift` line when it applies and when it ends. 404: unknown machine; 400: not the leak tester, a shift that is not a non-zero whole multiple of the tester's resolution, an `until` not after `at`, or an invalid time; 409: `at` in the past or `at`/`until` on a calendar boundary, or the run has finished.

shift.description: Pa/min added to the reading's mean: a non-zero whole multiple of the tester's resolution (0.001)

at.description: Simulation time, ISO 8601 with an offset or Z; the current time when left out

until.description: Simulation time after `at`, ISO 8601 with an offset or Z; the drift ends then or at the tester's next calibration, whichever comes first

id.description: Numbered with the failure injections, in acceptance order

shift.description: Added to every reading while active, in the tester's unit (Pa/min)

until.description: When it ends, unless a calibration ends it first

status.description: active: readings carry the shift; ended: by `until` or by a calibration

post.summary: Block a material lot, now or at a simulation time (skipped as if empty)
post.description: Scheduled as a simulation event at `at`, as failure injections are, and written to the event log as a `lot` event. A blocked lot is skipped as if it were empty: the consuming station starves with cause `MATERIAL:<material>` once no other lot of the material is left; a release wakes every starved station. The body is optional. 404: unknown lot; 400: invalid `at`; 409: `at` in the past or on a calendar boundary, or the run has finished.

post.summary: Mark operators absent for a later shift, whatever their roster draw says
post.description: Applied at the shift's start, which must be after the simulation time, so no running shift's staffing changes. The roster draw still happens (one per operator and shift), so every other shift is unchanged. The event log gets an `absence` event at the shift's start, before its `operator` events. Marking both ASM-01-qualified operators of a shift leaves ASM-01 `Idle` with cause `NO-OPERATOR`. 404: unknown operator or no such shift; 400: a malformed shift key, an operator not rostered on it, an id listed twice; 409: the shift has started, or the run has finished.

post.summary: Break a CNC's tool, now or at a simulation time
post.description: At `at` the tool's wear goes to end of life (1.0). A cycle in progress completes normally and draws its defect at wear 1.0; the tool is changed at the next start (`Setup` with cause `TOOL-CHANGE`), as at a natural end of life. No random draw is added or removed. The event log gets a `tool-breakage` event. The body is optional. 404: unknown machine; 400: not a CNC or an invalid `at`; 409: `at` in the past or on a calendar boundary, or the run has finished.

post.summary: Load a scenario timeline before the run starts
post.description: Loads a committed timeline (`name`) or one given inline (`timeline`), only while the run is idle and has no timeline, injection, drift or console action yet (body at most 512 KiB; at most 1000 entries). Every plant entry is accepted at the start time, injections then console actions, in timeline order, as a headless run of the same timeline gives them, so the event log is the headless one at any speed. `opcua-offline`, `modbus-silent`, `speed` and `pause` are applied by the pacer at their time and never touch the plant model. 404: no committed timeline of that name; 400: a document the schema refuses, a `dispatch` entry (headless only), an entry that does not fit the configuration or the run; 409: the run is not idle, has a timeline, an injection, drift or console action already, an earlier load failed part way, or the timeline names another seed, start or production mode. 413: a body over the limit.
